2. React Re-renders — Objects Created in Render
3. Over-Broad Effect Dependencies
4. Caching Opportunities
5. Redundant JSON Serialization (`assembler.js`)
6. DOM Layout Thrash — Textarea Auto-Height (`PromptOutput.jsx:261-266`)
7. Gallery Without Virtualization (`PromptOutput.jsx:1139-1164`)
sections.content:
Images load 20 at a time with no virtual scrolling. For large galleries this creates hundreds of mounted DOM nodes.

**Suggestion:** Add a "Load more" button or use `react-window`/`react-virtual` for the image grid. This is the biggest UX-visible issue at scale.

---

sections.title: Priority Order
sections.content:
| # | Issue | File | Effort | Impact |
|---|-------|------|--------|--------|
| 1 | `setTimeout` cleanup | `CharacterBuilder`, `PromptOutput`, `DirectorSection` | Low | Prevents stale state updates |
| 2 | Cache `fetchBankSlugs` | `App.jsx:307` | Low | Eliminates redundant network calls |
| 3 | Split hydration effect | `App.jsx:318-346` | Low | Reduces spurious re-renders |
| 4 | `useMemo` on mapped objects | `App.jsx:294-301` | Low | Stabilizes downstream memos |
| 5 | Debounce textarea height | `PromptOutput.jsx:261` | Low | Removes layout thrash on typing |
| 6 | Virtual scroll for gallery | `PromptOutput.jsx:1139` | Medium | Critical for large datasets |
| 7 | Chip diff comparison | `assembler.js` | Medium | CPU savings in hot path |

The `setTimeout` cleanup and `fetchBankSlugs` caching are the quickest wins — each is a 3-5 line change. The gallery virtualization is the most impactful for users with large image histories.
